newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo minister pleased with Washington talks -paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugo minister pleased with Washington talks -paper.

text.p: Yugoslav Finance Minister Tomica Raicevic has said that only a few issues remain to be resolved before the International Monetary Fund (IMF) decides on Yugoslavia's status, Belgrade papers reported on Tuesday.
The newspapers quoted him as saying upon returning from Washington on Monday evening that his talks with representatives of the IMF, World Bank and the U.S. government were "extremely successful".
"Practical steps were agreed in the World Bank," he said, adding that the bank's experts would be coming to Yugoslavia for talks on regulating future relations.

"Deputy U.S. finance secretary David Lipton showed great interest in the Yugoslav economic trends and economic system, especially regulations on foreign investment and privatisation," Raicevic was quoted as saying.

Yugoslavia regards a return to international financial institutions as a crucial step in efforts to secure foreign capital to repair its economy, devastated by three and a half years of international sanctions.
